Ticket #05 — Refund Processing

Difficulty: Medium

Context

You maintain a support tool for refunding payments. An authorized payment has approval to charge but has not been captured; a captured payment has collected funds. A partial refund returns some of those funds. Amounts use the integer units already stored in the payment ledger.

Practice report

Add payment p2 with amount 900 and state authorized. Request refund("p2", "rf2", 100).

Observation Current starter Expected
Service result "refunded" "rejected"
Refunded total 100 0
Payment state partially_refunded authorized

A refund ID identifies one refund request. An identical retry must have no additional effect; using that ID for different payment details is a conflict.

Acceptance Criteria

  • New refunds are eligible only for captured or partially_refunded payments. Unknown payments and payments in other states are rejected.
  • Amounts must be positive integers. Cumulative refunds cannot exceed the payment amount, including when several partial refunds are requested.
  • A successful request records one refund and sets the payment to partially_refunded or, at exact full refund, refunded.
  • An exact refund-ID replay returns already_refunded without another ledger effect. Reusing that ID for a different payment or amount is rejected.
  • Rejected requests leave payment state and refund records unchanged. A fully refunded payment cannot accept a new refund.

Out of Scope

Use the included ledger. Bank transfers, currency conversion, external refund providers, and asynchronous settlement are outside this ticket.

Investigation

Trace the report from payment lookup to the saved refund and payment state. Compare an uncaptured payment with a captured one, then test partial totals, exact settlement, over-refunds, and repeated IDs. Assert ledger contents as well as result strings.
